ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Liliʻuokalani

code.originalText: Five-month review: blood pressure, lipids, apixaban safety, cognition and plans for the months ahead

text.paragraph: Liliʻuokalani returns six weeks after her annual wellness visit, five months after the stroke. She has had no new neurological symptoms, no bleeding and no falls, and has finished arranging a new song. She takes apixaban twice daily without missed doses and does the balance exercises from the community program twice a week. Her home blood pressure averages 122/72. Her hepatitis C antibody test was negative, and her bone density scan showed osteopenia (lowest T-score -2.1 at the femoral neck) with a ten-year risk of hip fracture below the level at which medicine is advised. She would like her zoster and Tdap vaccines today. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-08-24; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 124/74, pulse 70 and regular; weight 57.8 kg
Normal speech, strength, fine finger movements and gait

Transient weakness and clumsiness of the right hand with word-finding difficulty, lasting about 20 minutes and fully resolved, the afternoon before the visit; suspected transient ischemic attack, ABCD2 score 5 (high risk); NIH Stroke Scale 0
S — Synthetic presenting problem; resolved into the stroke diagnosis when diffusion MRI showed a small infarct at the stroke clinic the next day. Not a claim about her real symptoms.

Minor ischemic stroke: a small acute infarct in the cortex of the left precentral gyrus (left middle cerebral artery territory) on diffusion MRI, embolic in pattern, with full recovery (NIH Stroke Scale 0); source found to be paroxysmal atrial fibrillation; synthetic modern episode linked to her documented death from a stroke
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the stroke clinic the day after the visit; the 1917 cause of death remains D.
Hypertension: told of borderline readings in past years and not treated; 156/88 mmHg at intake
S — Synthetic risk factor; no blood pressure from her lifetime is recorded in the cited sources.
Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation found on 30-day ambulatory monitoring after the stroke (six episodes, the longest 3 hours 10 minutes; burden about 3%); CHA2DS2-VASc 6, HAS-BLED 2
S — Synthetic finding on prolonged rhythm monitoring at five weeks.
Anterior nosebleed from the left side of the nasal septum four weeks after starting apixaban, stopped with pressure; hemoglobin unchanged; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent problem at an unscheduled visit; a common minor bleed on an anticoagulant, not a documented illness.

list.item:
Minor ischemic stroke (I63.412). No recurrence in five months; MoCA 27; LDL 62 mg/dL. [S]
Continue atorvastatin 40 mg; lipid panel yearly now that LDL is stable at goal.

Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on apixaban (I48.0). Hemoglobin 12.7 g/dL, platelets 226 and creatinine 0.88 mg/dL (creatinine clearance about 48 mL/min): apixaban 5 mg twice daily remains the right dose. CHA2DS2-VASc and HAS-BLED to be reviewed yearly. [S]
Continue apixaban 5 mg twice daily.
Blood count and kidney function again in about five months, or sooner with any illness.

Hypertension (I10). At goal: 124/74 in the clinic and 122/72 at home. [S]
Continue losartan 25 mg; potassium and creatinine with the next blood tests.

Osteopenia on bone density scan. Below the threshold for medicine; falls matter more on an anticoagulant. [S]
Calcium-rich foods, vitamin D, walking and the balance program; repeat scan in two to three years.

list.item: No recurrent stroke or transient ischemic attack. Outcome by 2026-08-24: None in five months on dual antiplatelets, then apixaban [S]
LDL cholesterol below 70 mg/dL. Outcome by 2026-04-20: 132 to 64 mg/dL on atorvastatin 40 mg [S]
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg at home and in the clinic. Outcome by 2026-06-15: 126/74 in the clinic; home average 124/72 [S]

Anticoagulation that is safe and taken as prescribed, without major bleeding. Outcome by 2026-08-24: Apixaban 5 mg twice daily from five weeks; one minor nosebleed, controlled at home and in the clinic; no missed doses [S]
